chapter: Vidals, blues, teachers and the Silver Leaf band
title: Arriving in New Orleans in 1909 and joining the Silver Leaf band in 1913
summary: He studied for two years, worked at a seed company, joined the Silver Leaf band, then formed Maple Leaf and his own band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: But anyhow, when you came to New Orleans, did you hear any bands before you started playing? Oh yeah. Did you go out and listen? Well sure. Who would you go and listen to before you?

I didn't know them then, you see. Oh, you didn't know their names? No, because I was living on Esplanade and Dupre. And I was working at Steckler Seed Company, see, but I was working in the yard then. And every now and then I'd go out and listen to the band playing. But I was taking music lessons during that year.
How long was it before you began to play with any of these bands?
I started playing exactly around 1912 and 1913.
So you had been down there about three years before you started playing? Fully two years.

Fully two years, because I went there in 1909, 1910. See, the later part of 1909 I went there. 1910 and 11, I was still taking lessons, you see. And 1913 I started playing with that band I'm telling you about. Which band?
Silver Leaf band. Oh, Silver Leaf. That was Baptiste then, you see.
And I played with them until they broke up. When they broke up, well then I thought we put up the Maple Leaf band. Then I played with them until they broke up. Then I put up my own band.
